text: Round Robin is a scheduling algorithm that gives each ready process a fixed time quantum. First Come First Served is a scheduling algorithm that runs processes in their arrival order. Shortest Job First is a scheduling algorithm that selects the process with the smallest estimated execution time. Priority Scheduling is a scheduling algorithm that selects a ready process according to its assigned priority.

FIFO Replacement is a page-replacement algorithm that removes the page loaded earliest into memory. LRU Replacement is a page-replacement algorithm that removes the page not accessed for the longest interval. Optimal Replacement is a page-replacement algorithm that removes the page whose next access is farthest in the future. Clock Replacement is a page-replacement algorithm that uses a circular pointer and reference bits to choose a page.

Merge Sort is a sorting algorithm that divides a sequence into halves and combines sorted results. Insertion Sort is a sorting algorithm that builds an ordered sequence by inserting each remaining element. Selection Sort is a sorting algorithm that repeatedly finds the smallest remaining element for the next position. Heap Sort is a sorting algorithm that organizes elements in a heap and extracts the largest remaining value.

DNS is a network protocol that resolves domain names into numerical addresses for clients. DHCP is a network protocol that assigns addressing configuration to clients for a lease period. HTTP is a network protocol that transfers requests and responses between web clients and servers. SMTP is a network protocol that transfers outgoing email messages between mail servers.

A stack is a data structure that removes the most recently inserted element first. A queue is a data structure that removes the earliest inserted element first. A tree is a data structure that connects parent and child nodes in a hierarchy. A graph is a data structure that represents vertices and edges between related entities.

Unit Testing is a software-testing method that checks the behavior of an individual program component. Integration Testing is a software-testing method that checks interactions between connected program components. Acceptance Testing is a software-testing method that checks whether a system meets specified user requirements. Regression Testing is a software-testing method that checks whether previously supported behavior survives a program change.

A full backup is a backup method that copies every selected file into a complete recovery set. An incremental backup is a backup method that copies files changed since the most recent backup operation. A differential backup is a backup method that copies files changed since the most recent full backup. A mirror backup is a backup method that maintains a duplicate of the current selected file collection.

Atomicity is a transaction property that makes a grouped operation succeed completely or take no effect. Consistency is a transaction property that keeps database states within their declared integrity rules. Isolation is a transaction property that controls the visibility of intermediate changes across concurrent transactions. Durability is a transaction property that retains committed changes even after a system failure.
